Subject: POC / Trial: Success criteria, RACI & next steps - Summit Health

Hi Erin — great to meet you on the call earlier. Thanks for walking us through the evaluation priorities. Per our discussion, wanted to capture next steps and get alignment on owners so we can start the POC kickoff next week.

Summary (high level)
- Objective: Validate Redwood inference for latency-sensitive NLP features in Summit Health patient portal (interaction routing + summarization).
- Rough success criteria: average 95th-percentile response latency < 350ms for 256-token context; semantic similarity precision > 0.88 on your labeled sample; integration readiness (API + auth) within 3 weeks.

Proposed evaluation plan / milestones
1) Kickoff & infra checklist (this week) — confirm cloud accounts, VPC peering approach, and data handling boundary. Owner: Summit infra (see below).
2) Baseline run (week 1) — Redwood deploys trial model + sample dataset, run synthetic traffic to validate latency and cost numbers. Owner: Redwood (Dev).
3) Integration test (week 2) — Summit devs integrate API, run end-to-end flows with masked PHI. Owner: Summit app team (Erin / Carlos).
4) Quality eval (week 3) — run labeled prompts, metric calculation, and stakeholder review. Owner: Joint.

Immediate asks for kickoff
- Can you confirm the infra contact and a preferred time for a 30-min kickoff?
- Please attach any network diagram or security checklist we should review in advance (we referenced peering vs. private link on the call).

I attached a short POC template and a sample network diagram to make it easier to fill in owners and timelines.

Next steps (my team)
- Dev (cc'd) will prepare a trial config and list of access requirements by EOD tomorrow.
- Lauren will coordinate contract/PO intake (if procurement is required).

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Hi Erin/Marissa — quick technical notes from our side to help Carlos plan network and account ownership: 

Trial infra options (we discussed both on the call)
A) Hosted Redwood trial (fastest)
- No network changes required from Summit — we provide API keys and you call our hosted endpoint over TLS.
- Data handling: masked/masked+hashed PHI recommended; we can sign a DATA Processing Addendum.
- Ownership: Redwood manages runtime; Summit owns app integration.

B) Private VPC peering (recommended for lower latency & isolation)
- Requires a peering or private link from Summit VPC to Redwood's trial environment.
- Ports: 443 outbound; for metrics we may request 9411 (for tracing) if you allow egress to our metrics collector.
- Account access: We need a service account and a minimal set of IAM permissions (list in attachment).
- Ownership: Summit infra to configure peering and security groups; Redwood to provide CIDR and test instances.

Telemetry & measurement plan
- We'll provide a test harness to measure p50, p95, and token-level cost.
- For quality eval, we'll run the labeled 1,200-example set you mentioned (please provide secure link). We can produce per-prompt confusion matrices and a short evaluation report at week 3.

Attachments I've put together:
- redwood-trial-reqs.txt (minimal IAM + firewall rules)
- trial-test-plan.md (end-to-end steps for baseline and integration tests)

I'll be online for the Thurs slot and can join the 30-min kickoff.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
